rationale: Lens: contract stability. The merge-safety.md gate-refusal section's LOAD-BEARING claims all trace true against internal/complete/materialize.go and complete.go: the panel gate (step 2.25) runs before runMaterialization; the snapshot + doc-sync/ADR-divergence gates run before any MaterializeStageCommit/PublishStageMarker/AdvanceBranchExpectedOld call, so a content-gate refusal returns with zero commits authored, no marker published, and the tip untouched at reviewed_head_sha (which is the genuine panel.json field name, internal/panel/panel.go:57); the retry's discriminator finds no marker, the panel gate re-runs and passes on the unchanged tip; --supersede-adr's placeholder pre-create is the only refusal-path disk write and only fires when that flag is passed. The POST-gate scoping (merge conflict / bd close = spec-127 territory) matches ADR-0041's own 'Honest scope' paragraph verbatim in spirit, and the section correctly stays silent on the mid-materialization marker/resume machinery (CAS races, index-reset failures), whose refusals name their own recovery. lifecycle-modes.md's cell-pinned agreement-table region (markers at lines 56-74) is genuinely untouched — the only hunk is the trailing cross-link paragraph at lines 199-204. ADR-0041, ADR-0037, and the ADR-0023 strike are all consistent with the new prose. HOWEVER: the workflow domain docs contradict the fourth in-scope amendment, ADR-0025's spec-128 R5.1 amendment, in four places — they document the SUPERSEDED pre-fix-round entanglement enumeration ('exactly session.json + issues.jsonl + worktree dir, therefore EMPTY today') that internal/next/guard.go's own doc comment explicitly calls out as the wrong original claim the bead-7 round-1 panel corrected. The delivered ComputeEntangleablePaths derives two CONDITIONAL blocking classes (.gitignore when the WorktreeRoot entry is absent; the recording events.ndjson/manifest.json paths when recording is enabled), gated on containment — the set is not unconditionally empty, and dirt on those paths still blocks. interfaces.md even attributes to ComputeEntangleablePaths exactly the two paths its comment says are EXCLUDED. This is the sweep's named failure mode (plausible-but-wrong prose the doc-sync gate can't catch) landing squarely on an ADR-amendment contradiction, so it must be fixed before merge. One smaller wording overpromise in merge-safety.md's retry sentence also needs tightening.
concrete_changes_required: Fix the four workflow-domain statements that contradict ADR-0025's spec-128 R5.1 amendment and internal/next/guard.go (ComputeEntangleablePaths): (1) .mindspec/domains/workflow/architecture.md §R5 — replace 'the entanglement is exactly `.mindspec/session.json` ... `.beads/issues.jsonl` ... and the new bead worktree directory — the claim-entangleable user-dirt set is therefore EMPTY today, so the invoking-worktree user-dirt block is REMOVED' with the delivered rule: two DERIVED conditional classes (.gitignore when cfg.WorktreeRoot's entry is absent at the claim anchor; the target spec's recording events.ndjson/manifest.json when recording is enabled), each included only when its resolved write target is contained in the invoking checkout's canonical toplevel; session.json/the worktree dir are excluded because gitignored; dirt ON an entangleable path still blocks, unrelated dirt no longer does (narrowed, not removed), and ignored dirt is named in a one-line stderr notice per the ADR amendment. Also drop 'even though the real, dynamic entanglement is empty' from the residual sentence. (2) workflow/overview.md line ~67 — 'a derived (today empty) entanglement set' misstates the conditional classes; say 'a derived, conditionally non-empty entanglement set' or equivalent. (3) workflow/runbook.md operational point 6 — 'the claim's actual (currently empty) entanglement set' same fix. (4) workflow/interfaces.md ComputeEntangleablePaths row — 'today: the gitignored session file and the already-exempt beads-artifact export — an empty user-dirt set' names exactly the two paths guard.go EXCLUDES; replace with the two derived classes + containment gate, and fix the EntangleableClaimPaths row's 'real, currently-empty entanglement' phrasing.

Tighten merge-safety.md's retry sentence, which promises more than the machinery guarantees: 'If the underlying skew persists (the override reason doesn't actually fix the content), the same gate refuses again on the retry with the same message; it never fails at a DIFFERENT gate (the panel stale-SHA check) than the one that refused first.' Two mechanical inaccuracies: (a) a retry that carries the override never refuses at that gate at all — AllowDocSkew/OverrideADR bypass the gate unconditionally and record the reason (materialize.go line ~273, handleADRGateOutcome); the reason is recorded, not evaluated, so 'the override reason doesn't actually fix the content -> same gate refuses again' describes a retry WITHOUT the flag; (b) the two content gates run sequentially (doc-sync first, returning before ADR-divergence runs), so a retry with --allow-doc-skew CAN fail at a genuinely different gate — the ADR-divergence gate seeing its first evaluation. Reword to promise only the real contract (mirroring ADR-0041 §1): a retry without the fix/override meets the identical content gate with the same message, and a refused run can never surface a false panel-staleness block — noting that overriding doc-sync may then surface the ADR-divergence gate, which is still a plain content-gate refusal with the same plain-retry recovery, never a staleness block.

findings.title: Workflow domain docs contradict ADR-0025's R5.1 amendment: the entanglement set is documented as the superseded 'exactly (a)(b)(c), empty today' claim in four places
findings.detail: ADR-0025's spec-128 amendment (on the spec branch since bead 7) and internal/next/guard.go both define the claim path's entanglement as two CONDITIONAL, containment-gated classes: .gitignore (when the WorktreeRoot entry is absent at the claim anchor) and the target spec's recording paths events.ndjson/manifest.json (when recording is enabled), plus the test residual — with .mindspec/session.json and the bead worktree directory explicitly EXCLUDED (guard.go's comment: 'the original "exactly (a)(b)(c), all gitignored/exempt" claim' is what the bead-7 round-1 panel found wrong). Bead 10's new docs state the superseded enumeration as live fact: workflow/architecture.md §R5 ('the entanglement is exactly .mindspec/session.json ... .beads/issues.jsonl ... and the new bead worktree directory — the claim-entangleable user-dirt set is therefore EMPTY today, so the invoking-worktree user-dirt block is REMOVED for this path' and 'the real, dynamic entanglement is empty'), overview.md line 67 ('derived (today empty) entanglement set'), runbook.md point 6 ('the claim's actual (currently empty) entanglement set'), and interfaces.md's ComputeEntangleablePaths row, which attributes to the function exactly the two paths it excludes. Operationally misleading: with recording enabled or a fresh checkout missing the .gitignore entry, dirt on those paths DOES block a claim, and the ADR-mandated stderr notice names ignored dirt — none of which the docs' 'removed/empty' framing admits. This is the exact plausible-but-wrong-prose failure mode this sweep's panel exists to catch, and a direct contradiction of one of the four in-scope ADR amendments.

findings.title: merge-safety.md's retry sentence promises 'same gate, same message; never a different gate' — more than the sequential-gate machinery guarantees
findings.detail: runMaterialization runs doc-sync first and returns on its failure before the ADR-divergence gate ever evaluates (materialize.go lines ~271-283); both overrides bypass their gate unconditionally (docResult.HasFailures() && opts.AllowDocSkew == ""; handleADRGateOutcome's opts.OverrideADR/SupersedeADR check) — the reason string is recorded, never evaluated. So (a) a retry carrying the override cannot 'refuse again at the same gate', and (b) a doc-skew-overridden retry can newly refuse at the ADR-divergence gate — literally 'a DIFFERENT gate than the one that refused first', though not the stale-SHA check. The guaranteed contract (per ADR-0041 §1: the retry meets the identical gate, never a false panel-staleness block, never masked dirt) is narrower than the sentence as written. All other claims in the new section verified true against the machinery: refusal-path commit/marker/tip immutability, no re-panel needed, POST-gate scoping to 127 territory matching ADR-0041's Honest-scope paragraph, and correct silence on the marker/resume machinery.

findings.title: Verified clean: lifecycle-modes.md pinned region untouched; ADR-0041/0037/0023 consistent; reviewed_head_sha terminology genuine
findings.detail: The agreement-table cell-pinned region (markers at lifecycle-modes.md lines 56-74) is untouched — the commit's only hunk there is the trailing cross-link paragraph (lines 199-204), whose characterization of the terminal row ('idle/done split') matches the existing row 72 text. merge-safety's 'byte-identical' tip phrasing mirrors ADR-0041 §1's own amended wording, and the ADR's §3(i) 'refusal guarantee, stated precisely' (unreachable loose objects excepted) is not contradicted at user-guide granularity. reviewed_head_sha is the real panel.json field (internal/panel/panel.go:57). The --supersede-adr placeholder pre-create is the sole refusal-path disk write and is flag-gated, so the 'mutates nothing' framing of a plain gate refusal holds for the flows the section describes.
